newsitem.title: USA: Dollar stumbles after reaching new heights vs mark and yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar stumbles after reaching new heights vs mark and yen.

text.p: The dollar seesawed Wednesday, powering to a 46-month high against the Japanese yen and a 30-month high against the German mark before falling in tandem with other U.S. markets.
Propelling the dollar's ascent was a recent string of healthy U.S. economic data and the market's desire to push the dollar above 1.60 marks, a key level not seen since July 1994.
"The psychological level of 1.60 marks was a magnet to the market," said Seth Garrett, chief dealer at Credit Suisse First Boston.

Public concern over the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin also aided the dollar. Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov said that Yeltsin had a "fairly serious illness" and should stay in the hospital until the end of the week because of the risk of complication in his pneumonia.
Traders bought dollars as a currency of refuge. Signs of political turmoil in Russia typically weaken the mark because of the close economic ties between Russian and Germany.

The dollar made its sixth consecutive high in as many trading days at 1.60 marks. But its inability to push past that level, along with significant losses in U.S. stocks and bonds, caused dealers to lock in profits by selling dollars.

"On New Years Eve, we were at 1.5380 marks and we went up to 1.60 today -- that is six pfennigs up without any retracement," said Hans Boman, chief spot dealer at Swedbank in New York. "But I don't think this will last for long."

The dollar closed lower at 1.5877 marks, compared with 1.5930 at the end of trade Tuesday. After hitting a 31-month high against the Swiss franc at 1.3808, the dollar closed at 1.3710, down from 1.3735 Tuesday.
Against the yen, the dollar fell from its 117.47 high to 116.82, off from Tuesday's 116.93 close.
Dealers said a Japanese newspaper report that quoted a Bank of Japan official as saying the central bank will maintain its low interest rate policy for the time being hurt the yen.
The British pound gained against the dollar after the Office for National Statistics reported surprisingly strong December jobs data in the United Kingdom.
"Sterling moved higher after the better-than-expected employment numbers today," said Christian Laland, a trader at Norwest Bank in Minneapolis.

The monthly monetary meeting between Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George was held Wednesday, but any decision regarding a speculated rise in interest rates is unlikely to become known until Thursday, traders said.
Higher UK rates would make pound-denominated investments more attractive to foreign investors.
Sterling ended higher at $1.6845 versus $1.6715 Tuesday.
In other trading, the dollar fell to 1.3415 Canadian dollars from C$1.3522 at the end of trade Tuesday.
